page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.26xlarge is a dedicated bare-metal or large virtualized compute instance belonging to the Local SSDs family. Built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 104 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It provides 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.69 GB of RAM per vCPU, and is paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps.

A primary hardware differentiator for the ecs.i3g.26xlarge is its bundled local storage subsystem, which incorporates 5759 GB of integrated local SSD storage. Unlike pure compute or standard memory-oriented server tiers that rely strictly on remote block volumes, this configuration couples substantial thread parallelism directly with high-capacity onboard solid-state storage. GPU accelerators are not present on this instance type.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling 5759 GB of local SSD storage together with 104 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of memory optimizes data-path efficiency by removing external storage network overhead. This makes it appropriate for I/O-intensive workloads requiring rapid local read and write operations, including distributed NoSQL and relational databases, large-scale search indexing, log processing, and real-time big data analytics pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.26xlarge is a storage-optimized instance within the Local SSDs family, running on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, delivering 104 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of RAM (3.69 GB per core). A central feature of this instance is its bundled 5759 GB local SSD storage array, which is complemented by a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no discrete GPUs. By co-locating significant compute density, ample memory, and high-capacity local disk space, the ecs.i3g.26xlarge avoids the latency and overhead of network-attached block devices. This hardware configuration is targeted directly at storage-heavy, parallelized workloads such as transactional database servers, distributed data stores, indexation engines, and extensive log analytics pipelines.
